activities.anchor: The answers that lost became named as heresies
activities.caption: pair each rejected answer with what it buys — and what it breaks
activities.name: christHeresyMatch

config.prompt: The grammatical emergencies — pair each named alternative with its trade:

pairs.right: the Son is a created being — solves monotheism, ends worship of Christ
the persons are masks of one actor — keeps monotheism, dissolves the relationships
three gods — keeps threeness, ends the Shema
'of the same substance' — the answer that carried the day

config.why: The doctrine's logic: nothing less than God could reunite humanity to God, so Christ must be divine — and the Spirit, who dwells in believers, must be too.

activities.anchor: Three layers of claim about Jesus
activities.caption: file each claim into its layer
activities.name: christLayersSort

config.prompt: History, faith, doctrine — file each claim:

items.label: a Galilean Jew, baptised by John, executed under Pontius Pilate — confirmed by Tacitus
teaching the imminent kingdom of God in parables
Paul's letters of the 50s already assume God raised him
the confession: Messiah ('anointed'), Son of God, the eternal Logos made flesh
Chalcedon 451: one person, fully God and fully human, two natures without confusion
the rejected alternatives — a merely adopted Jesus; a divine Christ only appearing human

config.why: The execution is among the best-attested facts of ancient religion; the resurrection is professed; the two-natures grammar is doctrine. Separating the layers is the method — without dismissing either.

activities.caption: order the Spirit's work, as doctrine tells it
activities.name: christSpiritOrder

config.prompt: From creation to the church's life — put the Spirit's work in order:
items: Present at creation — brooding over the waters
Inspiring the prophets and the scriptures
Descending at Pentecost (Acts 2: wind, fire, tongues — the church's birthday)
Ever after: sanctifying, guiding, making the sacraments effective
config.why: The Spirit's procession from the Father 'and the Son' — filioque, a single Latin word added unilaterally — helped split East from West in 1054. From Azusa Street (1906), Pentecostalism is now the fastest-growing Christian movement on Earth.

config.prompt: The New Testament's 27-book list first appears in exactly modern form in Athanasius' Easter letter — place that year on the century's scale:
config.why: 367 — Nicaea (325) debated the divinity of Christ, not the canon; the books emerged gradually, liturgically and decentrally, decades after Constantine.

activities.anchor: The movement's first decisive turn was sociological
activities.caption: scrub the arc from sect to schism
activities.name: christArcTimeline

events.title: Council of Jerusalem
events.text: Converts need not keep the Torah — circumcision, kashrut, Sabbath. A Jewish sect begins becoming a world religion.

events.title: Constantine legalises Christianity
events.text: The persecuted gains imperial standing; the establishment begins building.

events.title: Theodosius makes it official
events.text: Christianity becomes the empire's state religion; creeds, canon and basilicas follow.

events.title: East–West schism
events.text: Orthodox and Catholic divide over papal authority and the filioque — dogma carrying politics.

events.title: Luther's protest
events.text: Indulgences spark the Reformation; Protestantism's long fragmentation begins.

activities.caption: one meal, four readings — step into each
activities.name: christEucharistBranch

config.root: One meal, four theologies. You stand at the table as the words are spoken: 'this is my body.' Each reading below marks a real branch of the tradition — step through them:

start.text: The bread and the cup are held up. What, according to each branch, do the words accomplish?

choices.label: The substances truly change
choices.feedback: Catholic transubstantiation — the substances become Christ's body and blood, appearances aside.

choices.label: Christ is really present, in, with and under the elements
The faithful feed on Christ spiritually, from heaven
The meal is an obedient remembrance

transubstantiation.text: The Catholic position — and the doctrine around the table runs deep: papacy, magisterium, a church whose structure and sacrament rise or fall together.

real-presence.text: The Lutheran position — Luther refused to let the Reformation reduce the supper to a symbol, and the disagreement ran as deep as justification itself.

spiritual-presence.text: The Reformed position — the believer's heart ascends by faith; the elements signify what they convey.

memorialist.text: The memorialist position — common among Baptists and many free churches: the supper remembers a finished work.

config.why: All four are arguments about what the words at the table mean — which is why the Eucharist decided church structures as much as creeds did: papacy and magisterium, conciliar episcopacy, pastoral and congregational forms.

activities.anchor: Christmas grew into its popular cultural weight late
activities.caption: drag between the two feasts
activities.name: christFeastsCompare

config.prompt: Which feast does the calendar treat as its summit — drag the divider:

before.label: The December festival
before.text: The cultural heavyweight — its date and customs are medieval and Victorian accumulations, arriving by accretion rather than theology.

after.label: The Paschal feast
after.text: The theological centre — the resurrection claim is the faith's foundation, and every liturgical calendar treats this season as its summit.

config.why: The church's own ranking places the December festival below the Paschal feast — the year rehearses the faith's claims in time, and it peaks at the resurrection.
